title: The doctype declaration
learningObjectives: Identify and assemble the parts of a complete HTML document

understand.concept: The <!doctype html> declaration tells the browser to use standards mode. It is not an element and has no closing tag.
understand.whyItMatters: It avoids legacy quirks-mode behaviour and makes layout more predictable.
understand.analogy: A label describes how to interpret a document, but doctype is a machine-readable declaration.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a memory aid; HTML should not be interpreted literally through it.

explain.narrative: The <!doctype html> declaration tells the browser to use standards mode. It is not an element and has no closing tag.

examples.explanation: The heading appears; the declaration selects standards mode.
examples.expectedOutput: The heading appears; the declaration selects standards mode.

practise.guidedTask: Put <!doctype html> on the first line of a new document.
practise.independentTask: Create your own small page, open it in a browser and inspect the result.
hints: Check that each element is nested under the correct parent.
